title: Thin-tail usage heuristics (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad exploring thin-tail (infrequent/high-cost) user behavior and lightweight tier ideas. Want cheap onboarding for high-velocity users while protecting margin for weird edge-case sessions (long-context, multimodal returns, streaming).

Quick premise and goal:
- Most users are thin-tail: many sessions small, few sessions huge. We need pricing that doesn’t subsidize pathological sessions but still converts trial users.
- Build a small, easily-explainable hybrid product: session bundles + a tiny overage per-token when you exceed a safety cap.
- Explore unit-econ back-of-envelope to see thresholds for starter credits, burst allowances, and mini-retainers.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Model/hosting blended cost: $0.000012 per token generated (hosted + infra amortized). This is a conservative mid-2024 blended number across small 8xA100-ish pools after caching benefits.
- Request tokens (prompt + metadata) add another $0.000004 / token (parser/embedding/extra compute).
- Effective combined cost per token served: $0.000016 / token.
- Typical small session length: 450 tokens in + 300 tokens out = 750 total tokens.
- Heavy session (thin-tail) example: 10k tokens in + 20k tokens out = 30k tokens.
- Prefix caching reduces effective tokens for repeated contexts by ~30% for repeated customers. But thin-tail users rarely hit caching wins.

Per-session unit-econ:
- Small session (750 tokens) cost = 750 * $0.000016 = $0.012.
- Heavy session (30k tokens) cost = 30k * $0.000016 = $0.48.
- If customer does 100 small sessions/day => daily cost = 100 * $0.012 = $1.20 (~$36/mo per active user).
- If customer does 10 heavy sessions/day => daily cost = 10 * $0.48 = $4.80 (~$144/mo per heavy user).

Pricing levers to consider:
1) Free starter bundle: 1000 tokens/month free (cheap, converts).
   - Cost to Redwood per new user: 1000 * $0.000016 = $0.016 (no big deal if uptake is broad).
2) Session bundle (pack of N session credits): e.g., 100 session credits @ 750 tokens implied = 75k tokens. Discount vs payg.
3) Overage per-token above a session cap (e.g., 5k token soft cap per session).
4) Burst credits for first 3 sessions/day — encourage exploration.
5) Micro-retainer: $X/month gives Y guaranteed throughput & lower unit price. For thin-tail users, retainer should be tiny ($5-15/mo).

Sample tier sketches (for product thinking):
- Free: 1k tokens/mo free, 30s streaming limit, community model only. Good for discovery.
- Hobby: $8/mo -> 1M tokens/mo (or 1k session credits) — aimed at power users. Effective price per token = $0.000008 (markup).
- Micro-commit: $15/mo -> 2.5M tokens/mo, plus 10 burst credits that exempt session overage.
- Payg: $0.000025 per token with session soft cap 5k tokens; above that $0.000045 / token (covers tail).

Back-of-envelope margins under those tiers: assume infra cost $0.000016/token.
- Hobby (1M tokens for $8) revenue/token = $0.000008 -> negative margin relative to cost (loss leader). But many conversions expected; treat as acquisition spend.
- Micro-commit ($15 for 2.5M) rev/token = $0.000006 -> worse loss (only acceptable when subsidized by retention/upgrade funnel).
- Payg: $0.000025 revenue/token -> gross margin = (0.000025 - 0.000016)/0.000025 ≈ 36%.
- Overage price $0.000045 -> margin ≈ (0.000045 - 0.000016)/0.000045 ≈ 64%.

Session cap framing (psychology + protection):
- Soft cap (5k tokens/session) with friendly warning and one-click upgrade to burst credit or instant purchase reduces customer friction.
- Hard cap only for free/hobby tiers. Paid tiers get higher caps.

Burst credits model (cheap to implement):
- Give 3 free bursts per month for micro users. Bursts allow one session to go to 50k tokens at payg overage pricing for no extra friction. Converts heavy testers to paid tiers faster.
- Accounting: expected usage of burst credits is low; cost per burst ~ 50k * 0.000016 = $0.80. If 10% of users use a burst, amortize into price (tiny).

Starter credit economics:
- Offer $3 starter credit upon signup (expires in 30d). Cost to Redwood if fully consumed = $3. Effective tokens = $3 / 0.000016 ≈ 187,500 tokens. That's large; maybe cap starter conversion to lower dollar (e.g., $1).
- Alternative: starter credit expressed as session credits (e.g., 200 session credits @ 750 tokens each = 150k tokens — similar magnitude). But adding friction is OK.

Edge-case protection: thin-tail heavy sessions can leak significant cost if not gated. Options:
- Per-session soft cap + rate-limited overage pricing.
- Spike detection: if a single session exceeds 10x normal median for account, auto-flag & notify.
- Per-account daily token budget for free/hobby tiers.

Micro-scenarios (to sanity-check):
- 1k trial users: assume 15% convert to hobby, 3% convert to payg, 0.5% to micro-commit. Calculate expected revenue and cost.
  * 1000 signups -> 150 hobby ($8) = $1,200 rev; cost if fully consumed 1M tokens each (!) unrealistic. Realistic: hobby consumes 50k tokens/mo average. So cost per hobby user = 50k * 0.000016 = $0.80. Gross margin per hobby user = $8 - $0.80 = $7.20. Nice.
  * Payg (30 users) average 200k tokens/mo -> rev = 200k * 0.000025 = $5, cost = 200k * 0.000016 = $3.2 -> margin $1.8 / user.
  * Micro-commit (5 users) pay $15 -> usage 500k tokens/mo average -> cost = 500k * 0.000016 = $8; rev = $15 -> margin $7.
- This suggests published tier math must assume realistic usage per tier (not theoretical max).

Open questions / experiments to run:
- Measure actual token distribution from last 90d by cohort: median, 95th, 99th per-session and per-account per-day. Use that to set session caps and burst quantities.
- A/B test starter credit size: $1 vs $3 vs 200 session credits. Track activation (first 3 sessions), retention at 30d, conversion to paid.
- Test explicit per-session cap messaging vs per-account daily cap messaging. Which reduces surprise and increases trust?
- Explore embedding-only microplans (charged per-embedding call) to broaden SMB adoption.

Notes to self (implementation details):
- Billing integration needs fast lookups to determine session token bucket and burst credit eligibility; store session token counters in redis with per-account TTL.
- UI: show live token meter in session, with soft overlay when approaching cap. Allow one-click purchase of burst token pack.
- API: return header X-Token-Remaining and X-Session-Cap to assist SDKs.

Random brain-dumps:
- Could offer a "session insurance" micro-premium: $1/mo adds 3 extra bursts and raises soft cap to 20k. Good for SMB with occasional long exports.
- Consider per-tenant QoS + pricing for enterprises: flat committed throughput + lower unit price; keep payg for public developers.

Conclusion / next steps:
- Run distribution query + compute 50/95/99 percentiles and average tokens per session and per-account-day.
- Prototype UI & API headers for session tracking.
- Draft simple copy for free vs hobby vs payg that highlights simplicity ("Sessions included" + "Burst credits") rather than raw tokens.

End of scratchpad.

(Loose, rough, iterative — intended for personal use and quick iteration. Revisit after data pull.)
